payload.rationale: The question asks whether NHC records at least 4 Category 3+ Atlantic hurricanes in 2026 through Dec 1. Climatologically (1991–2020) the Atlantic averages about 3.2 major hurricanes per season; since 1995, roughly 15 of 31 seasons (~48%) reached 4 or more, with high year-to-year variance (0 in 2013, 7 in 2005/2020). No evidence about the actual 2026 season to date (named storms, majors already recorded, or ENSO state as of mid-September) was supplied, so I cannot condition on observed activity even though the peak of the season has passed by the information cutoff. Pre-season considerations pointed to a possible transition toward El Niño in late 2026 after the 2025–26 La Niña, which would tend to suppress late-season activity, while persistently warm Atlantic SSTs in recent years support above-normal intensity. Balancing base rates against a modestly less favorable ENSO expectation, I estimate ~40%. Too high if the season had been quiet through mid-September (few or no majors by then makes reaching 4 unlikely, since most major hurricanes form Aug–Oct) or if El Niño developed strongly. Too low if the season had already produced 3–4 majors by the cutoff, as recent hyperactive-leaning seasons (2020, 2024, 2025) show 4+ majors are common in the current warm-Atlantic regime; also, late-season Caribbean majors (e.g., Oct–Nov) frequently add to the count.
limitations: No supplied data on 2026 season activity to date, despite a mid-September cutoff
ENSO state and Atlantic SST conditions for 2026 not verified
Estimate relies on historical base rates rather than current observations
Resolution depends on NHC operational/post-season classification; upgrades or downgrades in post-analysis could affect the count
